items.claim: `buildSequences` throws `RangeError` on a long level run
items.note: Reproduced first: a one-level run of 1,000,000 characters threw inside vitest, and plain node already throws at 200k. The run's indices are now appended in a loop.

Reproduced first: 50k stray FSIs took 3.3 s. `pairIsolates` now pairs every initiator with its PDI in one stack pass and replaces `matchingPDI`. `resolveExplicit` computes it once and passes it to `paragraphLevelOf` for each FSI, and `buildSequences` makes its own linear pass. Pairing still reads the classes after overrides, so behavior is unchanged; the conformance tests still pass.

items.claim: `bidiClassOf`'s docstring misstates the defaults for unassigned code points
items.note: Confirmed by running it: an unassigned Currency Symbols point (U+20CF) gives `ET`, and U+FDD0 and U+E0080 give `BN`. The fix is in the generator's template and in the generated `tables.ts`, with a test pinning those values. The code was already right, so that test passed before the fix too; no failing test was possible for a doc-only defect.

items.claim: Text after a paragraph separator resolved with the earlier paragraph as context
items.note: A paragraph separator now ends its run of characters, and the start and end of a run never take their direction from the far side of one. I reproduced each of B's four cases with a test that failed before the fix: `a LF ! b` under rtl, alef LF `$1`, an NSM opening a paragraph, and a bracket pair spanning the separator.

items.claim: `reorder` accepted a range outside the analysis and returned characters that don't exist
items.note: `reorder` and `reorderLine` now throw a documented `RangeError` unless `0 <= start <= end <= length` and both are integers. This was a strict call nobody had made, so it is recorded in `docs/unruled.md` with no override. The callers in text and hud already keep their ranges in bounds.

items.claim: `ReorderedLine.levels` was documented as indexed by original index, but is indexed by line position
items.note: This one changes only documentation, so no test fails before it; the test that pins indexing by line position (`levels[i - start]`) went in with 8fd6b76d95.
